passage: In the lunch queue, Deepak saw two older boys take a Class Six child's money and threaten him if he told. Deepak's stomach twisted. He had fought with one of them last year, and he knew people would say he was just getting revenge. Mahima whispered, "Are you going to tell? They'll say you're a snitch." "I'm going to tell," said Deepak. "The little one is scared." He went to the class teacher. The teacher listened without interrupting and said, "Thank you for telling me. I won't assume anything. I'll deal with this today." Deepak's shoulders relaxed and Mahima squeezed his arm.

qa.q: What did the older boys take from the Class Six child?
qa.a: They took the child's money.

qa.q: What was Deepak feeling when he decided to tell the teacher?
qa.a: He was worried about being called a snitch, and uneasy about the younger child. He chose safety over what people might say.

qa.q: How did the teacher respond well?
qa.a: They listened, thanked him, did not assume his motives and promised to act that day. Adults should act on safety concerns.

qa.q: How might the Class Six child feel about Deepak telling?
qa.a: He was probably scared and may feel relieved that someone spoke up. Deepak acted for his safety.

grounding: A teenager reports something to an adult for safety, and the adult thanks him and listens without assuming motives.

passage:
"I read the group chat, Amma," said Charu. "They're posting nasty things about Gauri. I told the counsellor."
"Was that about a fight you had with them?" asked Lavanya.
"No. I felt sick reading it. I wasn't even angry. I just thought she shouldn't see it alone."
"Thank you for telling me. I'm proud you did."
"Some kids will say I'm a snitch."
"Maybe. But you did it for her safety, not to get them into trouble."
Charu breathed out. "The counsellor said she'd handle it carefully and not say who told."
"Good. Now come and eat."

qa.q: Who did Charu tell about the group chat?
qa.a: Charu told the counsellor.

qa.q: What was Charu feeling when reading the group chat?
qa.a: Charu felt sick and worried for Gauri, not angry, and wanted Gauri not to face it alone.

qa.q: What could Charu do if other kids call Charu a snitch?
qa.a: Charu can remember acting for someone's safety and talk with the counsellor or Amma again. Adults can help keep Charu's name private.

qa.q: How does Lavanya see Charu's reporting?
qa.a: She asks about motive gently, thanks Charu and says she's proud. She takes it as caring, not revenge.

grounding: A teenager reports hurtful messages out of concern for a classmate's safety, and a parent listens without assuming revenge.

passage:
In Class 10, I told the class teacher that Nilesh and his friends were planning to jump from the school's first-floor roof into the sandpit, for a video. I'd heard them planning it at lunch.
Part of me was scared someone would get hurt. But part of me, honestly, was still angry at Nilesh for a fight we'd had.
The teacher didn't ask why I was telling. She said, "Thank you. This matters." That same afternoon she spoke to the boys and called their parents, and the roof door was locked.
Nilesh called me a snitch for weeks. I felt bad. But later I realised, whatever my mixed reasons, someone could have broken their neck.
- Saurabh

qa.q: Where were Nilesh and his friends planning to jump into?
qa.a: The sandpit.

qa.q: What was Saurabh feeling when reporting Nilesh?
qa.a: Saurabh felt scared that someone would get hurt, and also some leftover anger about an old fight.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that was right?
qa.a: She thanked Saurabh, listened without assuming motives, and acted that same afternoon on the safety concern.

qa.q: How did Nilesh see Saurabh's report?
qa.a: Nilesh called Saurabh a snitch, seeing it as betrayal rather than protection.

grounding: The narrator recalls reporting a dangerous plan with mixed motives, and the teacher thanking the narrator and acting on safety.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Tuesday
Avni came to me today and reported that Riddhi had copied her maths homework. She seemed angry, and I know the two had a quarrel last week.
I thanked Avni for telling me and listened without assuming she was getting even. I said I'd look into it.
I checked both notebooks. The answers were very similar, including the same mistake in question five.
I spoke to Riddhi privately. She admitted she'd copied because she was stuck. I've arranged extra help for her.
I also spoke to Avni: I told her she did the right thing to tell me, and that it's okay to feel angry but I'll handle it now.
- Mrs Vasudha Menon

qa.q: Which question had the same mistake in both notebooks?
qa.a: Question five.

qa.q: What might Avni have been feeling when reporting Riddhi?
qa.a: Avni may have felt angry, both about the copying and the earlier quarrel, and wanted fairness.

qa.q: What did Mrs Menon do that was wise?
qa.a: She thanked Avni, didn't assume her motive, checked the facts, and dealt with the problem privately.

qa.q: How might Riddhi have felt when Mrs Menon spoke to her?
qa.a: Riddhi probably felt embarrassed but relieved to get help with maths.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a teenager reporting a peer, perhaps with mixed motives, and the adult thanking, listening and acting fairly.

passage:
Tuesday
Today I told the warden that Jyoti hasn't eaten dinner for four days and cries in the bathroom at night. I've been worried for a week.
Jyoti saw me coming out of the warden's office and said, "Why did you tell? It's none of your business." I felt terrible. Maybe she thinks I'm trying to get her in trouble because we argued about the fan last month.
But the warden thanked me and said I did the right thing. She talked to Jyoti this evening and called her parents. Jyoti's mother is coming tomorrow.
I'm still worried Jyoti will stay angry. But I'd rather she's angry and safe.
- Kalyani

qa.q: How many days had Jyoti not eaten dinner?
qa.a: Four days.

qa.q: What was Kalyani feeling after Jyoti confronted her?
qa.a: Kalyani felt terrible and torn, worried Jyoti thought the report was about the old argument.

qa.q: What did the warden do that was right?
qa.a: The warden thanked Kalyani, talked to Jyoti that evening, and called her parents.

qa.q: How might Jyoti see Kalyani's report later?
qa.a: Jyoti might eventually see it as care, not revenge, once she gets support.

grounding: A teenager's diary shows reporting a worrying change in a friend, and the adult thanking Kalyani and acting on safety the same day.

passage:
Anirban: Ma'am, sorry to message on the school portal. Rudra and two others are planning to climb the old gym roof after practice today to film a jump.
Kavitha Ma'am: Thank you for telling me, Anirban. Are you somewhere you can talk?
Anirban: Yes, library. Also... Rudra kicked me out of the team chat last week. So maybe you think I'm just getting back at him.
Kavitha Ma'am: I'm not deciding why you told me. What matters is that someone could get hurt. Did you see the plan yourself?
Anirban: He posted "gym roof 5pm, bring phone" before I got removed. I have a screenshot.
Kavitha Ma'am: Please send it. I'm going to Coach now, and the roof door will be locked before practice ends.
Kavitha Ma'am: The team chat thing sounds hurtful too. Want to talk about that at 4?
Anirban: ok. thank you ma'am 🙏
Kavitha Ma'am: 4:00, staffroom. See you there.

qa.q: Where was Anirban when he messaged?
qa.a: Anirban was in the library.

qa.q: What might Anirban be worried about when he mentions the team chat?
qa.a: Anirban seems worried that Kavitha Ma'am will think it's revenge, and is still hurt at being kicked out. The likeliest reading is mixed motives: real fear for safety alongside that sting.

qa.q: Which steps did Kavitha Ma'am take, and why do they work?
qa.a: She thanked Anirban, didn't judge the motive, asked for the evidence, went to Coach and had the roof door locked the same day, then offered time for the hurt.

qa.q: What would change if Kavitha Ma'am had focused on Anirban's motive?
qa.a: Anirban might have felt accused and stopped talking, and the roof jump could have gone ahead while they argued about why Anirban told.

grounding: It shows a teenager reporting a peer's risky plan with possibly mixed motives, and an adult who says thank you, listens without assuming and acts on safety the same day.
